tasks.title: Close the header gaps the SEC-001 audit proved on the wire
tasks.objective: SEC-001 blocked at three cycles with its core policy sound but four wire-verified gaps open. Fix them on top of agent/SEC-001-claude (658cc3d) without weakening the existing policy or tests.
tasks.humanItemNotAgentWork: A CI workflow is required so the wire suite cannot silently skip, but .github/ is a protected path and no agent may write it. Ken adds the workflow; the worker instead makes the wire suite FAIL LOUDLY (not skip) when a production build is missing, which is the part achievable in scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Trailing-slash requests (/sign-in/, /read/, /api/review/) carry the full security header set; today they 308 with ZERO headers, wire-verified, so the 'every route' claim is currently false.
The /sw.js overlay no longer applies to case variants (/SW.js, /Sw.Js); it must match the real worker script only.

The wire suite FAILS LOUDLY when no production build is present instead of skipping silently, unless an explicit opt-out env var is set; skipping by default is what let the only real-response evidence never run.
The wire suite derives its expectations from the resolved rule list rather than the exported constants, so de-registering a rule fails the wire tests and not only the unit tests.
A CSP report-to or report-uri endpoint, or a Report-Only companion policy, exists so a policy mistake in the credential-gated OAuth flow surfaces as a report instead of silent breakage.
Every existing security-headers test still passes unweakened, and the live Google OAuth round trip remains an explicitly open, credential-gated receipt that is NOT claimed closed.

tasks.title: Eliminate the blocked-delete data-loss window with a cross-tab write lock
tasks.objective: P0UI-001 blocked at three cycles because a write made in another tab while deleteDB sits blocked is destroyed when that tab closes, and the UI then certifies the device clear. The root fix needs the writers to participate, which the prior task was not permitted to touch. Build on agent/P0UI-001-claude (2ec3457).
tasks.scopeChange: web/lib/sync/store.ts moved from read-only to owned by Ken on 2026-08-13 so the writers can take the lock. This is the whole point of the successor task.
acceptanceCriteria: A write committed in a second tab AFTER the pending-queue check, while a deleteDB is blocked and queued, is never destroyed: either the delete cannot remain armed, or writers cannot commit while a clear is in progress.

The fix is taken by the writers (navigator.locks in lib/sync/store.ts and/or an idb blocking/versionchange handler that closes other connections), not only by the clear path; a lock taken solely in clear.ts is explicitly insufficient.

A regression test seeds the write AFTER the queue check while the delete is blocked, and fails against 2ec3457; the prior test only covered a write seeded before the check, which is why 68/68 passed while the bug was live.
After any interleaving that loses or could lose writing, the UI never renders a verified-clear claim; if the app cannot prove the device is clean it must say so.
The clear-device guidance no longer instructs the user to take an action that destroys data.
Fallback behaviour is defined and tested where navigator.locks is unavailable, and the fallback fails closed rather than destroying.
Every previously passing acceptance criterion of P0UI-001 still holds, and no existing test is weakened or deleted.

tasks.title: Complete protected sync and safe Settings controls
tasks.objective: Mount reconnect sync once inside the protected application, expose a current portable export, and provide one fail-closed clear-device-and-sign-out path while local storage remains account-unscoped.
acceptanceCriteria: The protected app layout mounts exactly one SyncRegistration; public and sign-in layouts do not mount it.
Settings exposes offline downloads, a portable export, and one clear-device-and-sign-out action in that order.
Ordinary sign-out that retains the unscoped IndexedDB vault is not offered until account/workspace namespacing lands.
Export synchronizes pending writes first and fails with an explicit incomplete-export message when offline, rejected, or unsynced; it never presents a stale server archive as current.
Clear-device refuses offline operation, failed sync clears nothing, successful clearing removes the app IndexedDB, matching app caches, and bible-brain:last-read while retaining unrelated caches.
If server sign-out succeeds but local clearing fails, the UI gives a shared-device warning and never claims the device was cleared.
This task does not claim the normal-sign-out cache-policy finding closed; arbitrary authenticated document/RSC caching remains a separate task.
verification: cd web; npm.cmd exec drizzle-kit check

tasks.title: Gate 0.3: Review page must use the real DB path and fail closed on missing setup
tasks.objective: app/(app)/review/page.tsx still calls the build-time seed bridge (lib/vault/seed.ts: getReview/getTeaching/getThreadRadar) instead of the already-existing authenticated DB path (lib/db/review.ts, already exercised by the tenant-isolation suite). This means (a) private data is compiled into the build output rather than read live per-user, and (b) a missing DATABASE_URL or empty account renders identically - an empty-looking page with no explanation, per BUILD_PLAN.md gate 0.3.
acceptanceCriteria: ReviewPage calls the authenticated lib/db/review.ts path (or an equivalent already-existing DB-backed function) for the signed-in user, not lib/vault/seed.ts.
A missing DATABASE_URL, a DB connection failure, or any other setup error renders a distinct, clearly labeled setup-incomplete state - not an empty page and not a generic 500.

A genuinely empty account (real DB, zero entries) still renders the existing empty-state copy for each section - the setup-incomplete state must be distinguishable from a legitimately empty account, never conflated.
The page requires an authenticated session (redirects or errors otherwise) rather than rendering for an anonymous request.

Existing review.module.css classes and the existing five sections (thread strength, radar, teaching, cold threads, orphans, mirror integrity) are preserved; only the data source and the new setup-incomplete branch change.
A new test proves: (a) setup-incomplete renders when the DB call throws/is unavailable, (b) a real empty account still renders the normal empty-state copy, not the setup-incomplete state.

tasks.title: Gate 0.5: verse-map load failure must fail closed, not silently misalign
tasks.objective: lib/bible/versemap.ts loadVerseMap() catches every failure (network error, non-ok response, bad JSON) and resolves to {} with no distinction from a successfully-loaded map confirming no divergence. alignChapter() then falls through to identity alignment for EVERY chapter when the map is unavailable - for a genuinely divergent chapter (Romans 14 ES / Romans 16 EN today, or any future addition to versemap.json) this silently renders the WRONG verse pairing in the parallel reader with no indication anything is wrong. The map failing to load must disable/warn on the parallel pane for potentially-divergent chapters, never silently guess.
acceptanceCriteria: loadVerseMap (or a caller-visible wrapper) distinguishes three states: map loaded and confirms this chapter does not diverge; map loaded and confirms this chapter DOES diverge (with alignment data); map failed to load (unknown divergence status) - these must NOT collapse into the same return shape.
chapterMayDiverge and alignChapter fail closed on load failure: a chapter that might diverge is never silently treated as identity-aligned when the map could not be loaded.

A documented, explicit failure surface exists for callers (e.g. a thrown error, a distinct return variant, or an exported failure flag) so the reader component can choose to disable the parallel pane and show a notice, rather than the current silent fallback.
The 1,187 non-divergent chapters remain a cheap identity zip when the map loads successfully - no added overhead or behavior change for the common case.
Existing Romans 14/16 alignment behavior (exact verse pairing, the explicit gap row for the Spanish 16:25 slot) is unchanged when the map loads successfully.

New tests prove: a network/fetch failure produces the distinct failure state, not a silent identity fallback; a non-ok HTTP response does the same; a malformed/unparseable JSON response does the same; the existing successful-load Romans 14/16 tests still pass unchanged.

tasks.title: Gate 0.4: offline navigation to unvisited chapters
tasks.objective: public/sw.js returns Response.error() when a navigation request misses the cache, so going offline and navigating to a chapter never visited before hard-fails even when that book Bible JSON is already cached. CODEX_AUDIT A-013. Offline reading is the core value of this app on a plane; it must either work or say plainly why it cannot.
acceptanceCriteria: An offline navigation to a never-visited chapter route, in a book whose Bible JSON IS cached, renders readable Scripture rather than a hard error - OR renders an explicit, honest offline notice naming what is missing. Silent failure is unacceptable; pick one and make it true.
If the approach is an app-shell fallback, the shell resolves the chapter from the URL and loads book data from the existing cache rather than refetching.
An offline navigation to a book whose data is NOT cached shows an explicit offline notice, never a blank page or a browser error page.
Online navigation behavior is completely unchanged - no added latency, no extra fetches, no cache-first staleness for HTML.
The service worker must NOT begin caching authenticated document/RSC responses as a side effect. CODEX_AUDIT A-014 stays open and must not be claimed closed here.
Tests prove the offline-unvisited-chapter path and the offline-uncached-book path distinctly, driving the real sw.js fetch handler logic rather than a reimplementation of it.

tasks.title: Gate 0.6: corpus builders must validate before destroying
tasks.objective: tools/build_bible.py and tools/build_spanish.py both call shutil.rmtree on the live output directory BEFORE parsing and validating the new corpus, and warn rather than exiting non-zero. A partial download or parser regression therefore replaces a known-good Bible with an incomplete one. CODEX_AUDIT A-004/A-027.
acceptanceCriteria: Neither builder deletes or overwrites the live corpus until the new corpus is fully built AND validated in a staging directory; the swap is atomic (or as close as the platform allows) and is the LAST step.

Validation is fail-closed and exits non-zero: 66 books, 1189 chapters, and the per-version verse count must match the declared expectation, with declared-omission exceptions listed explicitly rather than silently tolerated.
On any validation failure the live corpus is left byte-identical to its prior state, with a stderr report and a non-zero exit code.

VERIFIABILITY WITHOUT THE SOURCE CORPUS: the raw translation sources (tools/.cache) are gitignored and will NOT exist in a clean checkout. Extract validation into importable, testable functions and add tools/test_corpus_validation.py exercising them with SYNTHETIC fixtures (good corpus; short-by-one-chapter; missing book; undeclared empty verse). Do not require a real corpus rebuild to prove the fix.
Run the new test file and paste real output. If python is unavailable in the run environment, say so plainly and do NOT claim the tests passed.

The selected verse flows to NoteComposer as a canonical book.chapter.verse RefKey and persists on Entry.verse.

A verse reference survives capture -> local store -> sync payload -> export, verified end-to-end rather than asserted.
The parallel Spanish pane and the Romans 14/16 alignment path still render correctly with selection active; selection keys off the canonical reference, never the loop index.
lib/contracts.ts is NOT modified - Entry.verse already exists and the v1 contract stays byte-stable.
Tests prove keyboard selection, the RefKey round-trip through to export, and that chapter-level capture without a selection still works.

tasks.title: Phase 1: canonical passage-range contract (freeze before any v2 table)
tasks.objective: BUILD_PLAN Phase 1 requires a versification-aware canonical range type frozen BEFORE any v2 schema work, because every v2 table stores ranges and changing it later would be a destructive migration. Today only single-verse RefKey exists, which cannot express a literary unit like Genesis 1:1-2:3. This task builds ONLY the contract plus parsing/validation/formatting and tests - no tables, no API, no UI.
acceptanceCriteria: CanonicalRangeV1 { versificationId: "eng-protestant-66-31102-v1"; start: RefKey; end: RefKey } and DisplayReferenceV1 { canonicalRange; translationId; corpusReleaseId; mappedStart; mappedEnd } are defined verbatim per BUILD_PLAN 3.1, in a NEW versioned module. web/lib/contracts.ts must stay byte-stable.
Cross-chapter ranges within one book are supported (Genesis 1:1-2:3 round-trips). Cross-BOOK ranges are rejected.

Parsing/formatting round-trips exactly. Validation rejects reversed ranges, out-of-bounds chapters/verses checked against the real canon table, malformed keys with prefix/suffix junk, and cross-book ranges.
A single-verse range is representable and round-trips (start equals end).
Containment and overlap helpers exist and are tested, since the v2 evidence model will need them.

The SBL Romans 14/16 divergence is acknowledged: document in-module how a canonical range maps to a display reference through the versioned verse map, and test at least the Romans 16:25-27 to Spanish 14:24-26 mapping shape. Do NOT reimplement versemap.ts - import or reference it.
No database, no API route, no UI, no v2 tables. Contract and pure functions only.
